title: Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases: Servicing Policy Clause on One Open Case per Loan
content:
**Clause 1. One open case.** Under Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases, a loan has at most one open maturity case. Because a borrower holds only one reverse mortgage, the borrower of record has at most one open case (a limit of 1 open case per borrower).

**Clause 2. Opening condition.** A case is opened only when the borrower of record has no other case whose status is opened, awaiting HUD approval, deferred, due and payable, extension period or foreclosure referred. The test rests on Cedarline's own case records for that borrower of record, as they stand before the case is opened. What a caller says about other cases does not settle it.

**Clause 3. A further event on an open case.** When another documented maturity event occurs on a loan whose case is open, no second case is opened.

> *Retired wording, no longer in force:* "if the new event ranks higher in the order of precedence than the case's current event type, the case is reclassified to the new event type and event date while keeping its status and deadlines, and from then on the new type's settings govern (a death or sale removes any cure option)". This sentence has been superseded by the current basis and is not applied.

If the new event ranks lower, it is only noted on the case.

**Clause 4. Meaning of "open".** A case counts as open while its status is one of the plan's open-case statuses.

## Clause 2 at a glance

| Other case of the same borrower of record, by status | May a new case be opened? |
|---|---|
| opened, awaiting HUD approval, deferred, due and payable, extension period or foreclosure referred | no |
| none with any of those statuses | yes, as far as this clause goes |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A borrower's earlier case is recorded as cured. No other case of that borrower has an open status, so Clause 2 does not bar a new case.
- A borrower's case is in its extension period. A newly documented lower-ranking event on that loan opens no case and is only noted on the existing one (Clause 3).
